title: ITC's Dakshin Crowned India's Best South Indian Restaurant at National Awards
excerpt: The iconic Mumbai restaurant beat five other nominees at the Zee Zest Unlimit Awards 2026, as Kerala and South Indian cuisine enjoy a global moment.
body:
• ITC Hotels' Dakshin at ITC Grand Central in Mumbai won the Best South Indian Restaurant title at the Zee Zest Unlimit Awards 2026, beating five other nominees.
  • The award highlights the growing national recognition of South Indian cuisine, which nominees including Kerala-focused Restaurant Chef Pillai, Bengaluru's OOTA, and Mumbai's Benne helped elevate.
  • Dakshin has served rare regional recipes from Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Puducherry for decades, with its Iyer's Trolley achieving cult status.
  • The recognition comes amid a broader global wave of Kerala cuisine going international, with restaurants like Chatti in New York and Kerala Canteen in Leeds earning praise.

ITC Hotels' flagship South Indian restaurant Dakshin, located at ITC Grand Central in Mumbai, has been crowned India's Best South Indian Restaurant at the Zee Zest Unlimit Awards 2026, reinforcing a growing national appetite for the peninsula's diverse culinary traditions.

The award, announced at a ceremony in Mumbai earlier this year, saw Dakshin beat out five other nominees that collectively represented a new wave of South Indian fine dining: The Konkan Cafe (Mumbai), Benne (Mumbai), OOTA (Bengaluru), Restaurant Chef Pillai (Bengaluru), and Carnatic Cafe (Gurugram).

A Culinary Research Project on a Plate

Dakshin has operated for decades as something closer to an edible archive than a typical hotel restaurant. The kitchen curates rare, often disappearing recipes from across five South Indian states — Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Puducherry, and Tamil Nadu — presenting them with the hospitality precision ITC Hotels is known for.

Signature offerings like the Veinchina Mamsam (a slow-cooked Andhra meat preparation) and the Urulai Roast have built the restaurant's reputation among serious food enthusiasts. But it is the Iyer's Trolley — a rolling cart of hand-made mini adais, kunni paniyaaram, and banana dosas served tableside — that has achieved something approaching cult status in Mumbai's dining scene.

"A Culinary Research Project on a Plate Dakshin has operated for decades as something closer to an edible archive than a typical hotel restaurant."

The restaurant's design draws from the traditional Nallukettu bungalow architecture of Kerala, creating an atmosphere that transports diners to the peninsula's coastal and inland landscapes.

A Competitive Field Reflects South Indian Cuisine's Rise

The strength of the nominee list told its own story about South Indian cuisine's evolution beyond the familiar idli-dosa template. Each restaurant represented a distinct regional voice.

Benne, a relative newcomer in Mumbai's Bandra neighborhood, has made waves with its tribute to Bengaluru's legendary tiffin rooms, centering the Davanagere Benne Dosa — crispy, buttery, and served with spicy potato palya. OOTA, perched atop a Bengaluru microbrewery, takes diners on a tour of Karnataka's culinary micro-regions, from the fiery dishes of Saundatti to subtle Gowda community recipes sourced through extensive travel across the state.

Restaurant Chef Pillai, founded by Chef Suresh Pillai, has earned acclaim as a celebration of Kerala cuisine with a contemporary edge. Its signature Nirvana Fish — a whole fish pan-fried and then poached in coconut milk inside banana leaf — exemplifies the blend of rustic tradition and refined technique that defines the best of new South Indian cooking.

Carnatic Cafe in Gurugram has been quietly redefining what South Indian food can be in North India, with its Malleswaram 18th Cross dosa — thick, podi-coated, soft inside and crunchy outside — becoming a destination dish.

Kerala Cuisine Goes Global

Dakshin's win arrives during what may be the most ambitious moment for Kerala cuisine on the global stage. In New York, Chatti — named after the traditional clay pots central to Kerala's homes and toddy shops — debuted as Chef Regi Mathew's first international venture. Mathew, known for his acclaimed Kappa Chakka Kandhari restaurants in Chennai and Bengaluru, has built Chatti's menu around Kerala's abundant seafood, tropical produce, and masterful use of coconut, tamarind, and pepper.

In Leeds, England, Kerala Canteen achieved a Top 100 ranking among Indian restaurants in the UK within its first year of operation, earning the number three spot in Yorkshire alongside established names like the Michelin-recommended Prashad and the acclaimed Tharavadu. The restaurant's Kerala tapas concept — smaller plates designed for sharing — represents a modern rethinking of how South Indian food is served in the diaspora.

Beyond the Idli: What the Awards Signal

The Zee Zest Unlimit Awards span 33 categories across cuisine, beverages, and individual excellence. This year's winners included Naru Noodle Bar (Bengaluru) for Best Japanese Restaurant, Avatara (Mumbai) for Best Vegetarian Restaurant, and Chef Manish Mehrotra as the Unlimit Icon for his lifetime contribution to Indian cuisine.

For South Indian cuisine specifically, the recognition signals that India's food establishment is finally catching up to what home cooks across Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh have always known: the peninsula's culinary depth rivals any cuisine on the subcontinent, and its best restaurants deserve the same national spotlight long reserved for North Indian fine dining.
